# `shell/desktop/RealmOperatorMountDrain.js`

> **Source:** `webgpu-os/shell/desktop/RealmOperatorMountDrain.js`

_No file-level description found in source. Add one as a leading `/** ... */` JSDoc comment, or document it below._

## Functions

### `retainRealmOperatorMount(desktop, entry, cancel)`

Shell-private ownership of one exact Virtual Realm factory attempt. Desktop retains it before before-mount/open/factory awaits, never on the app object. cancel invokes the original mount/provisional cleanup, not an app-id lookup. The returned control record is kept only in the original mount continuation. It issues no lifecycle identity, app dependency or operator participant. Mount settlement is not cleanup. Drain first requests original cancellation, then waits for the complete mount continuation, retries/awaits its actual attached cleanup, and finally retires the original registry open's retained leases/quarantine. Window removal and host notification ACKs prove none of these. Failed cleanup stays retained across process removal and drain retries.

### `requestRealmOperatorMountDrain(entry)`

Start eventual cleanup after an ordinary/provisional/forced panel close. This deliberately does not make force-close UI await the application. A failed background attempt remains owned for the real operator drain.

### `drainRealmOperatorMounts(desktop)`

Called by Desktop's existing boot-owned operator drain, after it freezes new launches. Reject retained failures so OperatorContext cannot activate a replacement profile. Concurrent drains share one attempt; retries preserve failed records and do not replay already completed cleanup. No timeout, process-count observation or force-removal receipt substitutes for completion.

## Notes & Examples

### Command Bus Pattern

The OS uses a capability-gated command bus for inter-app and system communication. Apps register command handlers; the kernel routes commands based on capabilities. Commands can be local (same app), cross-app (with permission), or system-level (elevated).

**Example: Command registration and invocation**
```js
import { CommandBus } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/CommandBus.js';
import { Capability } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/Capability.js';

const bus = new CommandBus();

// Register a handler (requires 'ui' capability)
bus.register('myapp:openFile', async (path) => {
  const content = await storage.read(path);
  return { content, size: content.length };
}, { capability: 'storage' });

// Invoke locally
const result = await bus.invoke('myapp:openFile', '/docs/readme.md');

// Cross-app invocation (requires 'interop' capability)
const otherApp = bus.proxy('otherapp');
const data = await otherApp.invoke('otherapp:compute', input);

// Broadcast to all listening apps
bus.broadcast('system:themeChanged', { theme: 'dark' });
```

**See also:** [WebGPU OS Architecture](/webgpu-os/architecture.md) · [Security Model](/concepts/security-model.md)
